# Glossary {#sec-glossary}

Terms defined in the book, with the chapter where each is introduced. Every chapter is included, and
each term is listed once, under the chapter that teaches it.

| Term | Meaning | Introduced in |
|---|---|---|
| 5 A's | A five-step scaffold for brief counselling: assess, advise, agree, assist and arrange | *Assessing Diet & Talking to Patients* |
| 15-15 rule | Treatment of hypoglycaemia in a conscious patient: about 15 g of fast-acting glucose, then a recheck in 15 minutes | *Type 2 Diabetes* |
| 24-hour recall | A dietary assessment method in which the patient reports everything eaten and drunk the previous day; quick, but one day may not be a usual day | *Assessing Diet & Talking to Patients* |
| Absolute risk reduction | The actual difference in risk between the groups being compared, which depends on how high the starting (baseline) risk was | *Evidence vs Hype* |
| Absorption | Moving the products of digestion across the gut wall into the blood or lymph | *Digestion & Absorption* |
| Accessory organs | The salivary glands, liver, gallbladder and pancreas, which pour their juices into the gut along the way | *Digestion & Absorption* |
| Acetaldehyde | The carcinogenic breakdown product of alcohol; its build-up causes the alcohol flush | *Adulthood & Working Life* |
| Acetyl-CoA | The hub molecule where carbohydrate, fat and protein converge; it feeds the TCA cycle, fatty-acid synthesis or, in the fasting liver, ketone production | *Integrative Metabolism* |
| Acid-ash hypothesis | The belief that dietary protein leaches calcium from bone; with adequate calcium, higher protein is instead linked to fewer hip fractures | *Bone & Joint Health* |
| Acrylamide | A genotoxic carcinogen formed when starchy foods brown at high heat (the Maillard reaction) | *Macronutrients* |
| Acute disease- or injury-related malnutrition | Malnutrition with severe inflammation, as in acute illness or injury; the cachexia end (cachexia is illness-driven wasting of muscle, often with loss of fat) | *Undernutrition & Malnutrition* |
| Adaptive thermogenesis | The extra fall in energy expenditure after weight loss, beyond what the smaller body requires; it makes lost weight easy to regain | *Energy Balance* |
| Adipokines | The hormones and signalling proteins that fat tissue releases, such as adiponectin, which is insulin-sensitising and anti-inflammatory; in obesity adiponectin falls and pro-inflammatory adipokines rise | *Obesity & Metabolic Syndrome* |
| AgRP/NPY neurons | The accelerator neurons of the arcuate nucleus, which release agouti-related peptide (AgRP) and neuropeptide Y (NPY) and drive eating; AgRP blocks MC4R | *Appetite & Weight Regulation* |
| Albuminuria | Protein (albumin) leaking into the urine; graded A1–A3 and read with eGFR to stage CKD | *Chronic Kidney Disease* |
| Alcohol flush | Reddening after alcohol in people who carry an ALDH2 variant; it marks a build-up of acetaldehyde, and with continued drinking signals a raised risk of oesophageal cancer | *Adulthood & Working Life* |
| Amenorrhoea | The absence of menstrual periods; in a young athlete, it can signal low energy availability | *Childhood & Adolescence* |
| Amino acid | The building block of protein: a central carbon carrying an amino group, a carboxyl group, a hydrogen and a variable side chain; about 20 occur in protein | *Macronutrients* |
| Amino-acid pool | The crossroads where protein enters and leaves the metabolic map; the body has no storage protein, so drawing on it for fuel dismantles working tissue | *Integrative Metabolism* |
| Amphibolic | Both breaking down and building: describes the TCA cycle, whose intermediates are also drawn off to build other molecules and topped up from amino acids | *Integrative Metabolism* |
| Amylase | The enzyme that digests starch into smaller sugars, made by the salivary glands and the pancreas | *Digestion & Absorption* |
| Amylin | A satiety peptide released with insulin from the pancreas at each meal; it reduces meal size and slows the stomach | *Appetite & Weight Regulation* |
| Amyloid-β | An abnormal protein that accumulates in plaques between neurons in neurodegeneration | *Brain Health & Dementia* |
| Amylopectin | The branched form of starch; its many chain ends let it digest fast and raise blood glucose sharply | *Macronutrients* |
| Amylose | The straight-chain form of starch; with few chain ends it digests slowly, giving a gentler glucose rise | *Macronutrients* |
| Anabolic resistance | The weaker muscle-building response of ageing muscle to a given amount of protein, so that more protein is needed for the same effect | *Healthy Ageing* |
| Anabolic window | The period after exercise in which protein is claimed to be best used for muscle; it is far wider than marketed | *Adulthood & Working Life* |
| Anabolism | The building and storing pathways of metabolism, which diverge from the hub molecules and cost energy | *Integrative Metabolism* |
| Anaemia | A shortage of red blood cells or haemoglobin; iron, folate or B12 deficiency can cause it | *Micronutrients, Hydration & Electrolytes* |
| Androgens | The class of sex hormones that includes testosterone | *Evidence vs Hype* |
| Anorexia nervosa | Restriction of energy intake that leads to a low body weight, with an intense fear of gaining weight | *Childhood & Adolescence* |
| Anorexia of ageing | The fall in appetite and food intake that comes with age | *Healthy Ageing* |
| Anthropometry | Body measurements, such as weight, height and waist circumference, used as an objective anchor in assessment | *Assessing Diet & Talking to Patients* |
| Antibiotic-associated diarrhoea (AAD) | Diarrhoea caused by antibiotic disruption of the gut microbiome | *Gut Microbiome* |
| Antidiuretic hormone (ADH) | The hormone that reduces water loss in urine; with thirst, the everyday regulator of water balance | *Micronutrients, Hydration & Electrolytes* |
| Apolipoprotein B (apoB) | The protein carried on each LDL particle; it steps up with LDL-cholesterol around the final menstrual period | *Menopause & Midlife Health* |
| Arcuate nucleus | The sensing hub of the hypothalamic appetite thermostat, beside a gap in the blood–brain barrier, where hunger and fullness hormones in the blood are read | *Appetite & Weight Regulation* |
| Aspiration | Food or drink entering the airway; up to a third is silent, with no cough | *Undernutrition & Malnutrition* |
| Atherosclerosis | The build-up of plaque in the artery wall, where LDL cholesterol is deposited and inflames the wall; the plaque narrows the vessel and can rupture | *Cardiovascular Disease & Hypertension* |
| ATP | The cell's energy currency, made and spent continuously; the body holds only seconds' to minutes' worth, and its energy stores are glycogen and fat | *Integrative Metabolism* |
| Atrophic gastritis | A long-standing inflammation that thins the stomach lining, common in older age; the stomach makes less acid, so vitamin B12 cannot be split from food protein for absorption | *Healthy Ageing* |
| AUDIT-C | The consumption questions of the Alcohol Use Disorders Identification Test: a short questionnaire used to screen adults for hazardous or harmful drinking | *Adulthood & Working Life* |
| Available carbohydrate | The digestible carbohydrate in a food, the quantity that drives the glucose response | *Macronutrients* |
| Avoidant/restrictive food intake disorder (ARFID) | Restrictive eating driven by sensory aversion or fear, without concern about weight or shape | *Childhood & Adolescence* |
| Baby-led weaning | An approach to starting solids in which the infant feeds itself instead of being spoon-fed | *Infancy & Early Childhood* |
| Bacteriophage | A virus that infects bacteria; most viruses in the gut are bacteriophages | *Gut Microbiome* |
| Basal metabolic rate (BMR) | The energy needed to keep the body running at complete rest; the largest component of total energy expenditure (typically 60–70%), driven mainly by fat-free mass | *Energy Balance* |
| Beriberi | Thiamine (B1) deficiency, appearing where the staple is heavily refined; heart failure and oedema ("wet") or nerve damage ("dry") | *Micronutrients, Hydration & Electrolytes* |
| β-carotene | A precursor in orange and dark-green produce that the body converts to vitamin A as needed; safe from food because the conversion is self-limiting | *Micronutrients, Hydration & Electrolytes* |
| β-cell | An insulin-producing cell of the pancreas; in type 2 diabetes β-cells first compensate for insulin resistance, then fail | *Type 2 Diabetes* |
| β-oxidation | The breakdown of a fatty acid, inside the mitochondrion, into many molecules of acetyl-CoA | *Integrative Metabolism* |
| Bile salts | Detergents made by the liver from cholesterol that emulsify fat into tiny droplets that lipase can reach; about 95% are recycled | *Digestion & Absorption* |
| Binge-eating disorder | Recurrent binge eating (an unusually large amount of food in a short time, with a sense of loss of control) without regular compensation such as vomiting or fasting | *Childhood & Adolescence* |
| Bioavailability | The proportion of a nutrient in food that is absorbed | *Micronutrients, Hydration & Electrolytes* |
| Bioelectrical impedance (BIA) | An estimate of fat versus lean mass from a tiny electrical current, as in "body-fat" bathroom scales; easily thrown off by hydration | *Energy Balance* |
| Biotransformation | The liver's chemical conversion of drugs, hormones and metabolic waste into water-soluble forms, in two stages (Phase I and Phase II), so the kidneys can excrete them | *Evidence vs Hype* |
| Blinding | Keeping trial participants unaware of which treatment they receive | *Evidence vs Hype* |
| Body composition | What body weight is made of, in particular how much is muscle and how much is fat | *Energy Balance* |
| Body mass index (BMI) | Weight divided by height squared; a cheap population screening tool that cannot tell muscle from fat | *Energy Balance* |
| Bolus | The soft mass of chewed food and saliva that is swallowed | *Digestion & Absorption* |
| Bone remodelling | The continual turnover of bone, in which old bone is broken down (resorption) and new bone is laid down (formation) | *Menopause & Midlife Health* |
| Brush border | The surface of the cells lining the small intestine, formed by microvilli, where the last digestive enzymes sit | *Digestion & Absorption* |
| Buffered milk nutrient | A nutrient whose level in breast milk stays steady even when the mother runs low, at the cost of her own stores: iron, calcium, folate and zinc | *Pregnancy & Lactation* |
| Bulimia nervosa | Recurrent binge eating (an unusually large amount of food in a short time, with a sense of loss of control), followed by compensation such as vomiting, fasting or excessive exercise | *Childhood & Adolescence* |
| Butyrogenic | Yielding a relatively high proportion of butyrate when fermented, as resistant starch does | *Gut Microbiome* |
| Cahill phases | The staged hand-off of fuel supply in fasting: fed, post-absorptive (glycogen), early fasting (gluconeogenesis) and prolonged, protein-sparing ketosis | *Integrative Metabolism* |
| Calorimetry | Measurement of energy expenditure, directly from the heat the body produces or indirectly from the oxygen consumed and carbon dioxide produced | *Energy Balance* |
| Carbohydrate consistency | Keeping the timing and amount of carbohydrate steady from day to day; the counselling message for someone on a fixed insulin dose | *Type 2 Diabetes* |
| Cardiovascular-kidney-metabolic framing | The international framing that treats obesity, diabetes, cardiovascular disease and CKD as one connected disorder | *Chronic Kidney Disease* |
| Careful hand feeding | Offering food by hand for comfort; the approach preferred to tube feeding in advanced dementia | *Brain Health & Dementia* |
| Catabolism | The breaking-down pathways of metabolism, which converge on acetyl-CoA and release energy | *Integrative Metabolism* |
| Catch-up growth | Recovering growth lost after a nutritional setback; the capacity narrows with age | *Childhood & Adolescence* |
| Cellulose | A polysaccharide held together by β-links that no human enzyme can cut, so it passes through as dietary fibre | *Macronutrients* |
| Central (visceral) fat | Fat stored around the abdomen; it carries more metabolic risk than fat on the hips and thighs | *Energy Balance* |
| Central obesity | Excess fat carried around the abdomen, read at the bedside by waist circumference; in Asian adults, a waist of ≥90 cm in men or ≥80 cm in women | *Obesity & Metabolic Syndrome* |
| Cerebral small-vessel disease | Damage to the brain's small blood vessels, driven by chronic hypertension and worsened by diabetes, that produces lacunar strokes and white-matter changes | *Brain Health & Dementia* |
| Change talk | The patient voicing their own motivation to change | *Behaviour-Change Counselling* |
| Chelation | Binding of a drug by a mineral such as calcium or iron into a complex that cannot be absorbed | *Digestion & Absorption* |
| Chief cells | Stomach cells that make pepsin | *Digestion & Absorption* |
| Cholecystokinin (CCK) | A duodenal hormone released by fat and protein that increases pancreatic enzymes, contracts the gallbladder and slows gastric emptying | *Digestion & Absorption* |
| Cholesterol | A ring-shaped sterol that stabilises cell membranes and is the precursor of steroid hormones, bile acids and vitamin D | *Macronutrients* |
| Choline | A nutrient that supports foetal brain development; most pregnant women fall short of it | *Pregnancy & Lactation* |
| Chronic disease-related malnutrition | Malnutrition with mild-to-moderate inflammation, as in heart failure, cancer or kidney disease | *Undernutrition & Malnutrition* |
| Chronic kidney disease (CKD) | The progressive, largely silent loss of kidney function, defined and staged by its cause, eGFR and albuminuria | *Chronic Kidney Disease* |
| Chronic low-grade inflammation | A persistent, mild inflammatory state; in obesity it is driven by macrophages recruited into enlarged, stressed fat tissue | *Obesity & Metabolic Syndrome* |
| Chylomicron | A particle of reassembled fat packaged with cholesterol and protein in the enterocyte, too big for a blood capillary, so it reaches the blood through the lymph | *Digestion & Absorption* |
| Circadian misalignment | Eating, sleeping and working out of step with the body's internal clock, as in night-shift work | *Adulthood & Working Life* |
| *Cis* and *trans* | The two geometries of a fatty-acid double bond: *cis* kinks the chain (liquid oils); *trans* leaves it nearly straight, so *trans* fat behaves like saturated fat | *Macronutrients* |
| CKD–mineral and bone disease | The disorder of bone and blood vessels driven by retained phosphate and the failing kidney's loss of vitamin D activation | *Chronic Kidney Disease* |
| *Clostridioides difficile* infection | Severe colitis caused by a toxin-producing bacterium that proliferates when the gut microbiome is depleted, usually by antibiotics | *Gut Microbiome* |
| Cluster-randomised trial | A trial in which groups, not individuals, are assigned to each arm | *Micronutrients, Hydration & Electrolytes* |
| Coeliac disease | An immune reaction to gluten that damages the lining of the small intestine | *Digestion & Absorption* |
| Cofactor | A non-protein helper that an enzyme needs in order to work; many micronutrients act as cofactors | *Micronutrients, Hydration & Electrolytes* |
| Cognitive reserve | The brain's capacity to absorb damage before dementia shows | *Brain Health & Dementia* |
| Colonocyte | An epithelial cell lining the colon; its preferred fuel is butyrate | *Gut Microbiome* |
| Colostrum | The low-volume, antibody-dense milk of the first days after birth | *Infancy & Early Childhood* |
| Complementary foods | Solids given alongside breast milk or formula, from about 6 months | *Infancy & Early Childhood* |
| Complementary proteins | Plant proteins with different amino-acid shortfalls (cereals in lysine, legumes in methionine) that cover each other's gaps across the day, as rice and *dhal* do | *Macronutrients* |
| Complete protein | A protein not short of any essential amino acid, as animal proteins typically are | *Macronutrients* |
| Composite endpoint | Several outcomes counted together as one result | *Evidence vs Hype* |
| Confinement month | The first postpartum month and its prescribed diet, patterned by community (Chinese *zuo yue zi*, Malay *berpantang*, Indian practices) and resting on a heaty/cooling food model | *Pregnancy & Lactation* |
| Confounding | Distortion of an association by a third factor linked to both the exposure and the outcome | *Brain Health & Dementia* |
| Congenital leptin deficiency | A rare condition in which a child is born unable to make leptin, with extreme, early-onset obesity and relentless hunger; leptin injections rescue it | *Appetite & Weight Regulation* |
| Contemplation | The stage of change in which a patient is weighing a change up | *Behaviour-Change Counselling* |
| Controlled variable | A quantity that an integrated system of hormones and brain circuits defends, as it defends blood glucose and body temperature; appetite behaves this way | *Appetite & Weight Regulation* |
| Cori cycle | The return of lactate from muscle and red blood cells to the liver, which rebuilds it into glucose | *Integrative Metabolism* |
| Corrected age | A preterm infant's age counted from the due date, used to time solids | *Infancy & Early Childhood* |
| Cortisol | The main stress hormone | *Why Nutrition Matters* |
| Counter-regulatory hormones | The hormones that raise a falling blood glucose: glucagon and adrenaline act fast; cortisol and growth hormone act slowly | *Integrative Metabolism* |
| Cross-feeding | One microbial species living on the products of another, as when butyrate producers use the lactate and acetate released by primary fibre degraders | *Gut Microbiome* |
| Crossover concept | The shift of the exercise fuel mix from fat toward carbohydrate as intensity rises | *Integrative Metabolism* |
| CYP3A4 | The intestinal enzyme that normally breaks many drugs down before they are absorbed; grapefruit inhibits it | *Digestion & Absorption* |
| DASH pattern | Dietary Approaches to Stop Hypertension: a dietary pattern rich in fruit, vegetables and low-fat dairy that lowers blood pressure | *Why Nutrition Matters* |
| Defended range | The range of body weight the body defends, with a strong lower brake against starvation and a leaky upper one; no single set point has been located | *Appetite & Weight Regulation* |
| Dehydration | Too little body water, shown by thirst, dark concentrated urine, dizziness and reduced urine output | *Micronutrients, Hydration & Electrolytes* |
| Dementia | A clinical syndrome of acquired, progressive loss of memory and thinking severe enough to affect daily life | *Brain Health & Dementia* |
| Denaturation | The unfolding of a protein by heat or acid, which usually makes it easier to digest | *Macronutrients* |
| Diabetic ketoacidosis (DKA) | A medical emergency of near-total insulin deficiency, in which unchecked ketone production makes the blood acidic; defined by the acidosis, not the ketone level | *Integrative Metabolism* |
| Dialysis | Treatment that partly takes over the kidney's clearance of wastes and water once the kidney fails | *Chronic Kidney Disease* |
| Diet-dependent milk nutrient | A nutrient whose level in breast milk falls when the mother is deficient, so the baby bears the cost: vitamin B12, iodine, vitamin D and DHA | *Pregnancy & Lactation* |
| Diet history | A structured conversation about what a patient usually eats and drinks, walking through a typical day and probing high-yield areas such as drinks, snacks and portions | *Assessing Diet & Talking to Patients* |
| Dietary fibre | Carbohydrate that the small intestine cannot digest; much of it is fermented by gut bacteria | *Macronutrients* |
| Dietary guideline | A consensus synthesis in which an expert body weighs the whole evidence and translates it into advice a population can act on | *What a Healthy Diet Looks Like* |
| Dietary pattern | The diet taken as a whole, which predicts health better than any isolated nutrient | *Why Nutrition Matters* |
| Digestion | Breaking food into pieces small enough to absorb | *Digestion & Absorption* |
| Disaccharidases | Brush-border enzymes (lactase, sucrase, maltase) that split disaccharides into single sugars | *Digestion & Absorption* |
| Disaccharide | Two sugar units joined: sucrose, lactose or maltose | *Macronutrients* |
| Disease-related malnutrition | The chronic and acute disease-related types together, in which inflammation drives catabolism and blunts appetite, so it resists feeding alone | *Undernutrition & Malnutrition* |
| Division of responsibility | The feeding principle in which the parent decides what, when and where, and the child decides whether and how much | *Infancy & Early Childhood* |
| Docosahexaenoic acid (DHA) | A marine omega-3 fatty acid; in pregnancy it modestly reduces preterm birth | *Pregnancy & Lactation* |
| Doubly labelled water | A harmless isotope tracer, followed over one to two weeks, that measures total energy expenditure in free-living people; the gold standard | *Energy Balance* |
| Dual-allergen hypothesis | The hypothesis that the route of first exposure to a food decides the immune outcome: inflamed, eczematous skin sensitises, whereas meeting the food by mouth first builds tolerance | *Infancy & Early Childhood* |
| Duodenum | The first segment of the small intestine, which receives the pancreatic juice and the bile | *Digestion & Absorption* |
| DXA | Dual-energy X-ray absorptiometry: a low-dose X-ray scan that measures fat and lean mass; the accurate clinical and research reference for body composition | *Energy Balance* |
| Dysbiosis | Disruption of the normal microbial community, for example by broad-spectrum antibiotics | *Gut Microbiome* |
| Dyslipidaemia | An abnormal pattern of blood lipids, the cholesterol and triglycerides carried in lipoproteins | *Cardiovascular Disease & Hypertension* |
| Dysphagia | Difficulty swallowing | *Healthy Ageing* |
| Ectopic fat | Fat deposited inside organs such as the liver and muscle, instead of under the skin | *Obesity & Metabolic Syndrome* |
| Electrolytes | Charged minerals dissolved in body fluids, such as sodium and potassium | *Micronutrients, Hydration & Electrolytes* |
| Endothelium | The inner lining of a blood vessel | *Cardiovascular Disease & Hypertension* |
| Energy availability | The energy left for the body's own housekeeping after training has taken its share: intake minus the energy burned in exercise | *Childhood & Adolescence* |
| Energy balance | The relationship between the energy taken in as food and drink and the energy the body spends | *Energy Balance* |
| Enteral feeding | Tube feeding; a specialist rung of nutrition support | *Undernutrition & Malnutrition* |
| Enterocyte | An absorptive cell of the small intestine, with the brush border facing the gut contents and the far side facing blood and lymph | *Digestion & Absorption* |
| Enterohepatic circulation | The recycling of bile salts, about 95% of which are reabsorbed at the terminal ileum and returned to the liver | *Digestion & Absorption* |
| Enterotype | One of three discrete gut community types once proposed to classify everyone; now read as a continuous gradient | *Gut Microbiome* |
| Equol | The more active form of a soy isoflavone, made by gut bacteria that only some people carry | *Menopause & Midlife Health* |
| Essential amino acids | The nine or so amino acids the body cannot make, so they must come from the diet | *Macronutrients* |
| Essential fatty acids | The two fatty acids the body cannot make: linoleic acid (an omega-6) and α-linolenic acid (an omega-3) | *Macronutrients* |
| Estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) | An estimate of how well the kidneys filter, in categories G1–G5, read with albuminuria to stage CKD | *Chronic Kidney Disease* |
| Exclusive breastfeeding | Feeding breast milk only, with no other food or drink apart from vitamin drops or medicines | *Infancy & Early Childhood* |
| Exercise activity | Deliberate exercise, such as a run, a gym session or a swim | *Energy Balance* |
| Exercise-associated hyponatraemia | Low blood sodium during or after prolonged exercise, the over-hydration end of the hydration range; drinking only plain water in large amounts during endurance exercise can cause it | *Micronutrients, Hydration & Electrolytes* |
| External levers | What changes outside the body at a life stage: the food environment, activity, and who a person eats with | *Reading the Life Stages* |
| Faecal microbiota transplant (FMT) | Transfer of stool from a healthy donor to restore a depleted gut community; proven only for recurrent *C. difficile* infection | *Gut Microbiome* |
| Fat-free (lean) mass | Body mass other than fat; its muscle and organs are metabolically active and mainly determine basal metabolic rate | *Energy Balance* |
| Fat-soluble vitamins | Vitamins A, D, E and K: stored in fat and the liver, so deficiency develops slowly and megadoses can be toxic | *Micronutrients, Hydration & Electrolytes* |
| Fatty acid | A hydrocarbon chain (a water-hating tail) capped by a carboxyl group (a water-loving head); the building block of dietary fats | *Macronutrients* |
| Female-athlete triad | The linked trio of low energy availability, menstrual disturbance and impaired bone health | *Childhood & Adolescence* |
| Fermentation | Anaerobic metabolism by bacteria in the colon of food the host's enzymes could not digest | *Gut Microbiome* |
| Fermented food | A food made through desired microbial growth and enzymatic conversions; it need not contain live microbes when eaten | *Gut Microbiome* |
| Ferritin | A marker of iron status that falls before haemoglobin does, so it detects iron deficiency before anaemia | *Childhood & Adolescence* |
| Final menstrual period (FMP) | A woman's last menstrual period, the clinical reference point for dating menopause | *Menopause & Midlife Health* |
| FODMAPs | Fermentable oligosaccharides, disaccharides, monosaccharides and polyols: short-chain carbohydrates that are rapidly fermented in the colon | *Gut Microbiome* |
| Folic acid | The form of folate used in supplements and food fortification | *Micronutrients, Hydration & Electrolytes* |
| Food cues | The sight, smell and advertising of food, which trigger the reward system and can spark food-seeking even after a full meal | *Appetite & Weight Regulation* |
| Food diary | A dietary assessment method in which the patient records everything as it is eaten, for several days; rich in detail but prone to reactivity | *Assessing Diet & Talking to Patients* |
| Food environment | What is sold, priced, labelled and placed within reach of the people choosing food | *What a Healthy Diet Looks Like* |
| Food-first | Meeting micronutrient needs from a varied, mostly whole-food diet before turning to supplements | *Micronutrients, Hydration & Electrolytes* |
| Food fortification | Enriching familiar dishes (with egg, minced fish, tofu, milk powder, oil or full-fat dairy) so that each mouthful carries more energy and protein without more volume | *Undernutrition & Malnutrition* |
| Food-frequency questionnaire | A checklist of how often foods are eaten over months; captures the habitual pattern and ranks people, but estimates quantities poorly | *Assessing Diet & Talking to Patients* |
| Food insecurity | Not having reliable access to enough food; in older age it depends on physical access (shopping, carrying, cooking) as much as on money | *Healthy Ageing* |
| Food matrix | The physical structure of a food, including intact plant cell walls that slow the release of its sugars | *Macronutrients* |
| Food neophobia | Refusal of new foods on sight; a normal, usually transient toddler phase | *Infancy & Early Childhood* |
| Food synergy | The idea that foods act in combination, so a whole dietary pattern can predict health better than any nutrient studied in isolation | *What a Healthy Diet Looks Like* |
| Foremilk | The watery milk at the start of a feed | *Infancy & Early Childhood* |
| Fragility fracture | A break from a fall from standing height or less; any fragility fracture defines osteoporosis | *Bone & Joint Health* |
| Frailty | A clinical picture in older age whose features include unintentional weight loss, weakness, slow walking and exhaustion | *Healthy Ageing* |
| FRAX | A tool that estimates 10-year fracture probability, with Singapore-calibrated models | *Bone & Joint Health* |
| Free sugars | Added sugars plus the sugars in syrups and fruit juices, but not the sugar inside whole fruit; WHO advises less than 10% of energy | *Macronutrients* |
| Functional redundancy | The capacity of many different microbial species to perform the same function, so that people with different species share a functional core | *Gut Microbiome* |
| Galactagogue | A substance, often a food or herb, taken to raise breast-milk supply; the evidence that any does so is weak | *Pregnancy & Lactation* |
| Gastric emptying | The regulated passage of food from the stomach into the duodenum, slower after a fatty or large meal | *Digestion & Absorption* |
| Gastrin | A stomach hormone, released when protein arrives, that increases stomach acid | *Digestion & Absorption* |
| Gelatinisation | The swelling of starch granules during cooking, which makes starch easier to digest | *Macronutrients* |
| Genitourinary syndrome of menopause | Vaginal dryness and urinary symptoms after menopause; no food or supplement treats it | *Menopause & Midlife Health* |
| Gestational diabetes (GDM) | Diabetes that first appears in pregnancy, when the pancreas cannot compensate for the normal insulin resistance of pregnancy; it forecasts later type 2 diabetes | *Pregnancy & Lactation* |
| Ghrelin | The stomach hormone that drives hunger; it rises before meals, partly entrained to habitual meal times, and falls after eating | *Appetite & Weight Regulation* |
| GLIM criteria | The Global Leadership Initiative on Malnutrition's diagnostic rule, applied after a positive screen: at least one phenotypic criterion (weight loss, low BMI, reduced muscle mass) plus at least one aetiological criterion (reduced intake or absorption, or inflammation or disease burden) | *Undernutrition & Malnutrition* |
| GLP-1 receptor agonists | Engineered, long-acting versions of the gut satiety hormone GLP-1 (semaglutide; tirzepatide is a dual GIP/GLP-1 receptor agonist) that amplify satiety signalling; weight returns when they are stopped | *Appetite & Weight Regulation* |
| Glucagon | The pancreatic hormone that drives the liver to release glucose; the primary, rapid counter-regulatory hormone | *Integrative Metabolism* |
| Glucogenic | Able to become glucose; describes amino acids whose carbon enters the map as pyruvate or a TCA-cycle intermediate | *Integrative Metabolism* |
| Gluconeogenesis | The making of new glucose, by the liver and later the kidney, from lactate, glycerol and glucogenic amino acids | *Integrative Metabolism* |
| Glucose-6-phosphatase | The enzyme that frees glucose for export to the blood; present in the liver and kidney, absent from muscle | *Integrative Metabolism* |
| Glucose-6-phosphate (G6P) | Glucose tagged with a phosphate as it enters a cell, which traps it there; the carbohydrate roundabout of the metabolic map | *Integrative Metabolism* |
| Glucose–alanine cycle | The export of alanine from muscle to the liver, carrying carbon for new glucose and nitrogen for disposal as urea | *Integrative Metabolism* |
| Glucose-dependent insulinotropic polypeptide (GIP) | A duodenal hormone, released by glucose and fat, that signals the pancreas that glucose is coming; an incretin | *Digestion & Absorption* |
| Glucose sparing | The switch of most tissues to burning fat in a fast, leaving glucose for the brain and red blood cells, which depend on it | *Integrative Metabolism* |
| Glucose tolerance test (75 g) | Blood glucose measured fasting and 1 and 2 hours after a 75 g glucose drink; Singapore offers it in every pregnancy at 24–28 weeks | *Pregnancy & Lactation* |
| GLUT2 | The liver's glucose transporter, always present, which admits glucose in proportion to its concentration without insulin | *Integrative Metabolism* |
| GLUT4 | The glucose transporter of muscle and fat, which comes to the cell surface only when insulin signals | *Integrative Metabolism* |
| Glycaemic index (GI) | How much a portion of food containing 50 g of available carbohydrate raises blood glucose over about two hours, relative to glucose (100); low 55 or less, high 70 or more | *Macronutrients* |
| Glycaemic load (GL) | GI scaled to a real serving (GI × available carbohydrate in grams ÷ 100); low 10 or less, high 20 or more | *Macronutrients* |
| Glycogen | The animal store of carbohydrate, held in liver and muscle; structurally amylopectin taken further | *Macronutrients* |
| Glycogenesis | The building of glycogen from glucose | *Integrative Metabolism* |
| Glycogenolysis | The breakdown of glycogen to release glucose; the first source of blood glucose in a fast | *Integrative Metabolism* |
| Glycolysis | The splitting of glucose into two molecules of pyruvate, in the cytosol and without oxygen, yielding a little ATP | *Integrative Metabolism* |
| Goitre | A swollen thyroid, caused by iodine deficiency | *Micronutrients, Hydration & Electrolytes* |
| Gout | A metabolic disease of urate handling, in which uric acid crystals inflame the joint | *Bone & Joint Health* |
| Group 1 carcinogen | An agent classed as an established cause of cancer in humans; alcohol is one | *Adulthood & Working Life* |
| Gut–brain axis | The two-way signalling between the gut and the brain, through the vagus nerve, short-chain fatty acids, the immune system and microbial metabolites | *Gut Microbiome* |
| Gut microbiome | The community of microbes (mostly bacteria, with some archaea, fungi and viruses) living in the gut, densest in the colon | *Gut Microbiome* |
| Habit | Automatic, context-cued behaviour that runs with little conscious thought; a routine repeated in a consistent context takes weeks to months to become automatic | *Behaviour-Change Counselling* |
| Habitual intake | What a person usually eats over months, as opposed to on any one day | *Assessing Diet & Talking to Patients* |
| Haem iron | Iron bound in haem (the iron-containing part of haemoglobin and of a similar protein in muscle), which comes from meat, fish and poultry; well absorbed and little affected by the rest of the meal | *Micronutrients, Hydration & Electrolytes* |
| Haemodilution | A lower haemoglobin concentration caused by plasma volume expanding faster than red-cell mass; in mid-pregnancy it is usually not anaemia | *Pregnancy & Lactation* |
| Hard endpoint | An outcome that matters to the patient directly, such as a heart attack or death | *Evidence vs Hype* |
| HbA1c | A blood marker of average blood glucose over about three months | *Type 2 Diabetes* |
| Health Plan | The personalised plan that a resident enrolled in Healthier SG co-develops with their family doctor; the natural place to raise and refer a nutrition concern | *Interprofessional Practice & Referral* |
| Healthier SG | Singapore's national shift from reactive hospital care toward proactive, relationship-based prevention in primary care | *Why Nutrition Matters* |
| Healthier SG Chronic Tier | The Healthier SG subsidy framework (from 2024) that gives enrolled cardholders means-tested subsidies on selected chronic medications and other care components | *Interprofessional Practice & Referral* |
| Healthy-user bias | The tendency of people who choose one habit to differ in many other health-related ways, which can make the habit look protective in observational data | *Evidence vs Hype* |
| Hedonic hunger | Wanting food for pleasure with no energy need | *Appetite & Weight Regulation* |
| Hindmilk | The fat-rich milk later in a feed | *Infancy & Early Childhood* |
| Human milk oligosaccharides (HMOs) | Sugars in breast milk that the infant cannot digest and that selectively feed *Bifidobacterium* | *Gut Microbiome* |
| Hunger | The drive that starts a meal | *Appetite & Weight Regulation* |
| Hyperemesis gravidarum | Severe, persistent vomiting in pregnancy with weight loss, dehydration and ketosis; it needs referral | *Pregnancy & Lactation* |
| Hyperkalaemia | Raised blood potassium, which disturbs the heart's rhythm; in CKD a risk from potassium loads, potassium salt substitutes and potassium-raising drugs | *Chronic Kidney Disease* |
| Hypertension | Persistently raised blood pressure | *Cardiovascular Disease & Hypertension* |
| Hypoglycaemia | A dangerously low blood glucose | *Integrative Metabolism* |
| Hypophosphataemia | A low blood phosphate; the most dangerous feature of refeeding syndrome | *Integrative Metabolism* |
| Icosapent ethyl | A high-dose prescription drug used in selected patients, tested in the trial often cited as the "fish-oil trial"; its result does not extend to over-the-counter fish oil | *Cardiovascular Disease & Hypertension* |
| IDDSI | The International Dysphagia Diet Standardisation Initiative: a colour-coded 0–7 framework that gives texture levels the same meaning in every setting | *Undernutrition & Malnutrition* |
| If-then plan (implementation intention) | A plan that decides in advance when and where to act on a goal, such as "if the stall auntie forgets, then I'll remind her *siu dai*" | *Behaviour-Change Counselling* |
| IGF-1 (insulin-like growth factor 1) | A growth-signalling hormone closely related to insulin; dairy raises it | *Evidence vs Hype* |
| Ileal brake | Feedback from the GLP-1/PYY cells at the far end of the small intestine that slows the stomach and signals fullness | *Appetite & Weight Regulation* |
| Incretin effect | The larger insulin response to glucose eaten than to the same glucose given intravenously, carried by the gut hormones GIP and GLP-1 | *Digestion & Absorption* |
| Infant botulism | Illness caused when *Clostridium botulinum* spores, for example from honey, colonise the immature infant gut and make toxin | *Infancy & Early Childhood* |
| Insoluble fibre | Bulking fibre, as in wholegrain bran and vegetable skins, that adds bulk and aids regularity | *Macronutrients* |
| Insulin resistance | A reduced response of the body's cells to insulin; at first the pancreas compensates by making more insulin to keep blood glucose normal; with central fat, the hub of the metabolic syndrome | *Obesity & Metabolic Syndrome* |
| Insulin sensitivity | How well the body clears glucose in response to insulin | *Why Nutrition Matters* |
| Insulin-to-glucagon ratio | The balance of the two pancreatic hormones that sets the body to store fuel (high, after a meal) or mobilise it (low, between meals) | *Integrative Metabolism* |
| Internal drivers | What changes inside the body at a life stage: growth, hormones and physiology | *Reading the Life Stages* |
| Intrinsic factor | A secretion of the stomach's parietal cells needed to absorb vitamin B12 at the terminal ileum | *Digestion & Absorption* |
| Isoflavones | The chief phytoestrogens of soy | *Menopause & Midlife Health* |
| Keshan disease | A disease of heart muscle caused by selenium deficiency, which depends on soil selenium | *Micronutrients, Hydration & Electrolytes* |
| Ketogenic (amino acid) | Entering the map only as acetyl-CoA, so unable to become glucose; a few amino acids are purely ketogenic | *Integrative Metabolism* |
| Ketone bodies (ketones) | β-hydroxybutyrate, acetoacetate and acetone: water-soluble fuels the fasting liver makes from surplus acetyl-CoA and exports to other organs, including the brain | *Integrative Metabolism* |
| Ketosis | A raised level of ketones in the blood, as in a prolonged fast or on a ketogenic diet; restrained by residual insulin, with a normal blood pH | *Integrative Metabolism* |
| Koilonychia | Spoon-shaped nails, a sign of iron deficiency | *Micronutrients, Hydration & Electrolytes* |
| Lactase deficiency | Making little lactase after childhood; the norm in most of the world's adults, and not a disease | *Digestion & Absorption* |
| Lactate | The product of pyruvate when oxygen is scarce; making it regenerates what glycolysis needs to keep running | *Integrative Metabolism* |
| Lacteal | A lymph vessel that takes up chylomicrons from the gut | *Digestion & Absorption* |
| Lactose intolerance | Symptoms (bloating, wind) from a given amount of lactose; most people tolerate the lactose in about a cup of milk | *Digestion & Absorption* |
| Lacunar stroke | A small, deep brain infarct caused by cerebral small-vessel disease | *Brain Health & Dementia* |
| LDL (low-density lipoprotein) | The lipoprotein that delivers cholesterol; it drives atherosclerosis when it builds up, and saturated fat raises it | *Macronutrients* |
| Leaching | Soaking cut vegetables, then boiling them and discarding the water, to lower their potassium | *Chronic Kidney Disease* |
| Lean body mass | The body's functional, non-fat tissue (muscle and organ protein), broken down in a sustained energy deficit | *Assessing Diet & Talking to Patients* |
| Leptin | A hormone released by body fat in rough proportion to the amount stored; a long-term fuel gauge the brain reads to regulate appetite and defend body weight | *Energy Balance* |
| Leptin resistance | The brain's failure to respond to the high leptin of common obesity, which is why leptin therapy does not treat it | *Appetite & Weight Regulation* |
| Liking | The actual pleasure of a food, driven by opioid "hotspots" separate from dopamine | *Appetite & Weight Regulation* |
| Lipase | The pancreatic enzyme, working with colipase, that digests fat | *Digestion & Absorption* |
| Lipolysis | The breakdown of stored fat, releasing fatty acids and glycerol from adipose tissue | *Integrative Metabolism* |
| Lipoprotein | A particle that carries fats through the blood, in which they cannot dissolve; the classes are chylomicrons, VLDL, LDL and HDL | *Macronutrients* |
| Lipoprotein lipase | The enzyme on adipose capillaries that strips triglyceride from circulating lipoproteins | *Integrative Metabolism* |
| Lipotoxicity | The harm done when free fatty acids and ectopic lipid spill over into non-fat tissues; in liver and muscle it disrupts insulin signalling | *Obesity & Metabolic Syndrome* |
| Macronutrients | The nutrients needed in gram quantities that supply energy: carbohydrate, fat and protein | *Macronutrients* |
| Macrosomia | Foetal overgrowth, driven in gestational diabetes by the foetus's own raised insulin | *Pregnancy & Lactation* |
| Maillard reaction | The high-heat browning of food that adds flavour; in starchy foods it forms acrylamide | *Macronutrients* |
| Malnutrition | In clinical screening and diagnosis, the deficit state (undernutrition): a disease state in which a deficit of energy, protein or micronutrients measurably changes body composition and function and worsens outcomes. In the broad sense, overnutrition and undernutrition are its two tails | *Undernutrition & Malnutrition* |
| Malnutrition Universal Screening Tool (MUST) | A validated screen for malnutrition risk that combines BMI, recent unplanned weight loss and acute illness stopping intake | *Assessing Diet & Talking to Patients* |
| Mechanical loading | Exercise that stresses the skeleton through impact or resistance; the strongest lever on bone at menopause | *Menopause & Midlife Health* |
| Medical food | A regulatory product category with a lower bar than a medicine; the label is not evidence that the product works | *Brain Health & Dementia* |
| Medical nutrition therapy (MNT) | An individualised, therapeutic nutrition plan for a medical condition, delivered by a registered dietitian through a cycle of assessment, diagnosis, intervention and monitoring | *Interprofessional Practice & Referral* |
| Mediterranean pattern | A dietary pattern built on olive oil, nuts, legumes, fish and vegetables | *Why Nutrition Matters* |
| Melanocortin-4 receptor (MC4R) | The receptor where the appetite accelerator and brake are summed: α-MSH activates it to reduce eating and AgRP blocks it to increase eating; MC4R mutations are the commonest single-gene cause of severe obesity | *Appetite & Weight Regulation* |
| Menarche | The first menstrual period | *Childhood & Adolescence* |
| Mendelian randomisation | A study design that uses genetic variants to remove the biases of observational comparisons, such as the sick "abstainers" in alcohol studies | *Adulthood & Working Life* |
| Menopausal hormone therapy | Prescribed hormones that replace the oestrogen the ovaries no longer make | *Menopause & Midlife Health* |
| Menopause | The reproductive transition in which the ovaries wind down and oestrogen falls, dated clinically to the final menstrual period | *Menopause & Midlife Health* |
| Metabolic-bariatric surgery | Weight-loss surgery; a specialist tier of obesity treatment for selected patients, added to lifestyle change | *Obesity & Metabolic Syndrome* |
| Metabolic syndrome | The tendency for five cardiometabolic problems (central obesity, raised triglycerides, low HDL cholesterol, raised blood pressure, raised fasting glucose) to appear together; diagnosed when any three are present | *Obesity & Metabolic Syndrome* |
| Metagenome | The collective gene catalogue of the gut microbes, about 150 times the size of the human genome | *Gut Microbiome* |
| Methanogenic archaea | Archaea that consume hydrogen to produce methane, such as *Methanobrevibacter smithii* | *Gut Microbiome* |
| Microbial diversity | The number of different species present in a microbial community and how evenly they are represented | *Gut Microbiome* |
| Micronutrients | The vitamins and minerals: needed in milligram or microgram amounts, they supply almost no energy but enable the body's reactions | *Micronutrients, Hydration & Electrolytes* |
| Microvilli | The fuzz of tiny projections on each lining cell of the small intestine; together they form the brush border | *Digestion & Absorption* |
| Mifflin–St Jeor equation | An equation that estimates basal metabolic rate from weight, height, age and sex | *Energy Balance* |
| Migrating motor complex | A cyclical wave between meals, triggered by motilin, that sweeps leftovers and bacteria onward roughly every 1–2 hours | *Digestion & Absorption* |
| Mild cognitive impairment | A decline in memory or thinking that falls short of dementia | *Brain Health & Dementia* |
| Milk allergy | An immune reaction to milk protein, unrelated to lactase | *Digestion & Absorption* |
| MIND diet | A blend of Mediterranean and DASH eating that emphasises leafy greens, berries, nuts, wholegrains, fish and olive oil | *Brain Health & Dementia* |
| Mixed feeding | Giving an infant both breast milk and formula | *Infancy & Early Childhood* |
| Mixed micelles | Clusters of bile salts and the products of fat digestion that ferry those products to the brush border | *Digestion & Absorption* |
| Mixed pathology | More than one disease process in the same brain, typically neurodegeneration with small-vessel disease; the rule in older people | *Brain Health & Dementia* |
| Monosaccharide | A single sugar unit: glucose, fructose or galactose | *Macronutrients* |
| Motilin | A small-intestinal hormone, released during fasting, that drives the migrating motor complex | *Digestion & Absorption* |
| Motivational interviewing (MI) | A collaborative way of talking that draws out the patient's own reasons to change instead of supplying the clinician's | *Behaviour-Change Counselling* |
| mTORC1 | Mechanistic target of rapamycin complex 1, a growth-sensing protein complex at the hub of a signalling pathway inside cells | *Evidence vs Hype* |
| Mucus barrier | The layer of mucus that keeps gut bacteria away from the epithelial surface | *Gut Microbiome* |
| Multidomain programme | A prevention programme that combines diet, exercise, cognitive activity and vascular monitoring | *Brain Health & Dementia* |
| My Healthy Plate | Singapore's "quarter, quarter, half" plate: a quarter wholegrains, a quarter protein and half fruit and vegetables | *Why Nutrition Matters* |
| Mycobiome | The fungal members of the gut microbial community | *Gut Microbiome* |
| NADPH | A building currency, made by the pentose phosphate pathway and spent on synthesis, such as of fatty acids, and on antioxidant defence | *Integrative Metabolism* |
| Nephron | One of the kidney's filtering units; CKD is their progressive loss | *Chronic Kidney Disease* |
| Neural-tube defect | A birth defect of the brain or spinal cord, such as spina bifida, risked when folate is too low as the neural tube closes, about four weeks after conception | *Micronutrients, Hydration & Electrolytes* |
| Neurodegeneration | The accumulation of abnormal proteins (amyloid-β, tau) with loss of synapses and neurons and brain atrophy; the dominant process in Alzheimer's disease | *Brain Health & Dementia* |
| Neuroglycopenic symptoms | Symptoms of the brain running short of glucose: confusion, slurred speech and eventually loss of consciousness | *Integrative Metabolism* |
| Non-communicable disease (NCD) | A chronic disease that is not passed from person to person, such as cardiovascular disease, type 2 diabetes, cancer or chronic respiratory disease | *Why Nutrition Matters* |
| Non-exercise activity thermogenesis (NEAT) | The energy spent on all movement other than deliberate exercise, such as walking, fidgeting, taking the stairs and standing; it varies enormously between people | *Energy Balance* |
| Non-haem iron | Iron not bound in haem, which comes from plants, eggs and fortified foods; poorly and variably absorbed, depending on the rest of the meal | *Micronutrients, Hydration & Electrolytes* |
| Non-sugar sweeteners | Sugar substitutes, as in "diet" drinks; the WHO advises against relying on them for weight control | *Obesity & Metabolic Syndrome* |
| Numeric threshold | A population limit set by a dietary guideline, such as free sugars under 10% of energy or salt under 5 g a day | *What a Healthy Diet Looks Like* |
| Nutri-Grade | Singapore's A–D front-of-pack grade on drinks, based on sugar and saturated fat | *Why Nutrition Matters* |
| Nutrient density | The amount of nutrients a food supplies for its energy | *Healthy Ageing* |
| Nutrition Information Panel | The nutrient table on a packaged food or drink, quoted per serving and per 100 g or 100 ml | *Assessing Diet & Talking to Patients* |
| Nutrition screening | A fast, low-skill filter that anyone can apply to flag malnutrition risk and trigger referral; it is not the assessment or the diagnosis | *Undernutrition & Malnutrition* |
| OARS | The four micro-skills of motivational interviewing: open questions, affirmations, reflective listening and summaries | *Behaviour-Change Counselling* |
| Obesogenic food environment | A food environment in which palatable, energy-dense food is cheap, abundant and always in view | *Appetite & Weight Regulation* |
| Observational study | A study that records what people already do, without assigning a treatment; a prospective cohort study is one | *Evidence vs Hype* |
| Oedema | Swelling from fluid collecting in the tissues | *Chronic Kidney Disease* |
| Oestrogen-receptor-positive | Describes a breast cancer whose growth is sensitive to oestrogen | *Menopause & Midlife Health* |
| Open-label trial | A trial in which participants know which treatment they are receiving | *Micronutrients, Hydration & Electrolytes* |
| Oral nutritional supplements (ONS) | Supplement drinks, used as an evidence-based add-on when food-based measures fall short | *Undernutrition & Malnutrition* |
| Oral rehydration salts (ORS) | A low-strength mix of glucose and sodium (75 mmol/L each in the WHO formula) that rehydrates by mouth because SGLT1 keeps working in diarrhoea | *Digestion & Absorption* |
| Orthorexia | An obsessive fixation on "clean eating"; a recognised pattern, not yet a formal diagnosis | *Childhood & Adolescence* |
| OSTA | An Asian screen, based on age and weight, that flags who needs a bone scan | *Bone & Joint Health* |
| Osteoarthritis | Worn, painful joint cartilage; the commonest arthritis | *Bone & Joint Health* |
| Osteoblast | A bone-forming cell that lays down new bone | *Bone & Joint Health* |
| Osteoclast | A cell that resorbs (breaks down) old bone | *Bone & Joint Health* |
| Osteogenic | Bone-building; exercise is most osteogenic in early puberty | *Childhood & Adolescence* |
| Osteomalacia | Vitamin D deficiency in adults, with soft, aching bones | *Micronutrients, Hydration & Electrolytes* |
| Osteoporosis | Low bone density, silent until a bone breaks; defined by a DXA T-score of −2.5 or below or any fragility fracture | *Bone & Joint Health* |
| Oxalate | A compound in some greens, notably spinach, that binds calcium and reduces its absorption | *Micronutrients, Hydration & Electrolytes* |
| Oxidative phosphorylation | The process on the inner mitochondrial membrane that makes most of the cell's ATP, using oxygen as the final acceptor of electrons | *Integrative Metabolism* |
| Parenteral feeding | Intravenous feeding; a specialist rung of nutrition support | *Undernutrition & Malnutrition* |
| Parietal cells | Stomach cells that make hydrochloric acid and intrinsic factor | *Digestion & Absorption* |
| Peak bone mass | The most bone a person ever has | *Childhood & Adolescence* |
| Peak height velocity | The fastest growth of the pubertal growth spurt, the fastest since the first year of life | *Childhood & Adolescence* |
| Pellagra | Niacin (B3) deficiency, remembered as the "3 Ds": dermatitis, diarrhoea and dementia | *Micronutrients, Hydration & Electrolytes* |
| Pentose phosphate pathway | The exit from glucose-6-phosphate that yields NADPH and ribose, not ATP | *Integrative Metabolism* |
| Pepsin | The stomach enzyme, made by chief cells, that cuts protein into peptides | *Digestion & Absorption* |
| Peptidases | Brush-border enzymes that finish the digestion of protein | *Digestion & Absorption* |
| Peptide bond | The bond, formed in a condensation reaction, that links amino acids into protein chains | *Macronutrients* |
| Perimenopause | The years of fluctuating ovarian hormones before the final menstrual period | *Menopause & Midlife Health* |
| Peristalsis | Travelling waves of muscle contraction that push the bolus forward | *Digestion & Absorption* |
| Person-first language | Language that names the person before the condition ("a person with obesity", not "an obese patient") | *Obesity & Metabolic Syndrome* |
| Personal fat threshold | The individual level of body fat beyond which a person develops type 2 diabetes; people of Asian descent can cross it at a lower BMI than Western cut-offs assume | *Type 2 Diabetes* |
| Phosphate additives | Inorganic phosphates used to preserve and improve processed foods; absorbed almost completely and often not on the label | *Chronic Kidney Disease* |
| Phosphate binder | A drug taken with meals to manage retained phosphate in CKD; prescribing it is a specialist decision | *Chronic Kidney Disease* |
| Phospholipid | A lipid with two fatty acids and a phosphate head on glycerol; amphipathic, it self-assembles into the lipid bilayer of cell membranes | *Macronutrients* |
| Physical activity (PA) | The most variable component of total energy expenditure, made up of exercise activity and NEAT | *Energy Balance* |
| Physical-activity level (PAL) | A factor that multiplies basal metabolic rate to estimate total energy expenditure, from about 1.4 (sedentary) to 2.0 (very active) | *Energy Balance* |
| Phytate | A compound in wholegrains, legumes and nuts that binds iron and zinc and reduces their absorption | *Micronutrients, Hydration & Electrolytes* |
| Phytoestrogens | Plant compounds, chiefly the soy isoflavones, that weakly mimic oestrogen | *Menopause & Midlife Health* |
| Pica | Craving for non-foods, classically ice; a sign of iron deficiency | *Micronutrients, Hydration & Electrolytes* |
| Plate method | A low-numeracy tool that sets the proportions of the plate; Singapore's version is My Healthy Plate (a quarter wholegrains, a quarter protein, half fruit and vegetables) | *Type 2 Diabetes* |
| Plate model | A dietary guideline expressed for individuals as the proportions of a plate, such as My Healthy Plate | *What a Healthy Diet Looks Like* |
| Polypharmacy | Taking five or more medicines | *Healthy Ageing* |
| Polysaccharide | A long chain of sugar units, such as starch, glycogen or cellulose | *Macronutrients* |
| POMC/CART neurons | The brake neurons of the arcuate nucleus, which make pro-opiomelanocortin (POMC) and cocaine- and amphetamine-regulated transcript (CART) and suppress eating; POMC is cut into α-MSH, the "stop" signal that activates MC4R | *Appetite & Weight Regulation* |
| Population-attributable estimate | The share of cases associated with a set of risk factors, assuming they are fully causal and could be eliminated from the whole population; a theoretical ceiling, not an individual's risk reduction | *Brain Health & Dementia* |
| Portal vein | The vein that carries absorbed sugars and amino acids from the gut to the liver | *Digestion & Absorption* |
| Postbiotic | A preparation of inanimate microbes and/or their components that confers a health benefit | *Gut Microbiome* |
| Postmenopause | The years after the final menstrual period | *Menopause & Midlife Health* |
| Pre-contemplation | The stage of change in which a patient has not yet thought about changing | *Behaviour-Change Counselling* |
| Pre-eclampsia | A hypertensive disorder of pregnancy | *Pregnancy & Lactation* |
| Pre-Ramadan review | A consultation, ideally weeks before Ramadan, to risk-stratify a patient with diabetes and adjust medication for fasting | *Type 2 Diabetes* |
| Prebiotic | A substrate selectively used by host microorganisms conferring a health benefit; mostly fibres | *Gut Microbiome* |
| Prediabetes | The phase in which blood glucose has started to rise but is not yet in the diabetes range; it is usually long and silent, and not everyone progresses | *Type 2 Diabetes* |
| Preformed vitamin A | Ready-made vitamin A, found in liver, egg yolk and dairy; teratogenic at high doses | *Micronutrients, Hydration & Electrolytes* |
| Preparation (stage of change) | The stage of change in which a patient is ready to plan a change | *Behaviour-Change Counselling* |
| Primary prevention | Preventing disease before it develops | *Cardiovascular Disease & Hypertension* |
| Primary structure | The sequence of amino acids in a protein chain | *Macronutrients* |
| Probiotic | Live microorganisms that, when administered in adequate amounts, confer a health benefit | *Gut Microbiome* |
| Prospective cohort study | A study that records what people eat (or another exposure) and follows them forward for years to see who develops disease | *Evidence vs Hype* |
| Protein-energy wasting | Undernutrition layered on kidney disease: low body and muscle mass, poor intake and abnormal blood chemistry; common on dialysis and linked to death | *Chronic Kidney Disease* |
| Protein quality | How well a protein's amino acids match human needs and how digestible it is, scored by PDCAAS or its FAO-preferred successor DIAAS | *Macronutrients* |
| Proton-pump inhibitor (PPI) | A drug that suppresses stomach acid; long-term use adds to the risk of vitamin B12 deficiency | *Healthy Ageing* |
| Psychobiotic | A microbe or microbial product claimed to improve mental health | *Gut Microbiome* |
| Purines | Compounds, rich in red and organ meat and some seafood, that the body breaks down into urate | *Bone & Joint Health* |
| Pyruvate | The product of glycolysis and a junction: its carbon can become lactate, alanine, oxaloacetate or, irreversibly, acetyl-CoA | *Integrative Metabolism* |
| PYY (peptide YY) | A satiety peptide from cells lower down the small intestine; at normal post-meal levels it cuts food intake by about a third | *Appetite & Weight Regulation* |
| Quaternary structure | The assembly of several protein chains (subunits) into one molecule, as in haemoglobin's four | *Macronutrients* |
| Randomised controlled trial (RCT) | A study in which chance decides who receives the treatment and who receives the comparison | *Evidence vs Hype* |
| RANKL | A signalling molecule that promotes bone resorption by osteoclasts; it rises when oestrogen falls | *Menopause & Midlife Health* |
| Reactivity | Eating differently because intake is being recorded; the signature bias of a food diary | *Assessing Diet & Talking to Patients* |
| Recall bias | Error in reported intake that arises because the report depends on memory | *Assessing Diet & Talking to Patients* |
| Reciprocal regulation | The coordination of opposing pathways so that one runs while its opposite idles, avoiding a futile cycle | *Integrative Metabolism* |
| Recognise and refer | The posture of the life-stage chapters: anticipate the stage-defining need, recognise the red flag, advise what is simple and safe, and refer | *Reading the Life Stages* |
| Recommended Dietary Allowance (RDA) | A population reference intake adequate for nearly all healthy adults; for protein about 0.8 g/kg/day, a floor rather than an optimum | *Adulthood & Working Life* |
| Refeeding syndrome | A dangerous fall in blood phosphate, potassium and magnesium when a starved or severely malnourished person is fed again and the insulin surge drives them into cells | *Integrative Metabolism* |
| Refined starch | Starch that is digested fast and stripped of fibre, as in white rice and white bread | *Macronutrients* |
| Relative energy deficiency in sport | The broader form of the female-athlete triad, arising from low energy availability | *Childhood & Adolescence* |
| Relative risk reduction | A change expressed as a share of the starting risk, such as "30% lower" | *Evidence vs Hype* |
| Remission (type 2 diabetes) | Blood glucose held below the diabetes range off glucose-lowering drugs (formally, an HbA1c below the diabetes range sustained off them); it is not cure, because it can relapse, so monitoring continues | *Type 2 Diabetes* |
| Resistance exercise | Muscle-strengthening exercise against a load; the necessary stimulus for keeping muscle | *Adulthood & Working Life* |
| Resistant starch | Starch that escapes digestion in the small intestine and behaves partly like fibre; it forms when cooked starch is chilled | *Macronutrients* |
| Respiratory quotient (RQ) | The ratio of carbon dioxide produced to oxygen consumed: about 1.0 when burning carbohydrate, about 0.7 when burning fat, around 0.85 on a mixed diet | *Energy Balance* |
| Responsive feeding | Feeding that follows the child's hunger and fullness cues | *Infancy & Early Childhood* |
| Retrogradation | The change in cooked starch on chilling by which some of it becomes resistant starch | *Macronutrients* |
| Reverse causation | An association produced when the outcome changes the exposure, as when people who become ill cut back on coffee | *Evidence vs Hype* |
| Reverse cholesterol transport | The carrying of cholesterol from the tissues back to the liver by HDL | *Integrative Metabolism* |
| Reward system | The brain system that drives eating because food is pleasurable and available; it can override fullness | *Appetite & Weight Regulation* |
| Rheumatoid arthritis | An autoimmune joint disease managed with disease-modifying drugs | *Bone & Joint Health* |
| Rickets | Vitamin D deficiency in children, with bowed legs or knock-knees | *Micronutrients, Hydration & Electrolytes* |
| Righting reflex | The near-irresistible urge to jump in and fix, warn or lecture; it feels helpful but reliably provokes resistance | *Behaviour-Change Counselling* |
| Risk-tiered (targets) | Set according to estimated cardiovascular risk: a clinician estimates the risk (in Singapore, with SG-FRS-2023), and the ACE guidance gives the individual's blood-pressure or cholesterol target | *Cardiovascular Disease & Hypertension* |
| Sarcopenia | The age-related loss of muscle strength and mass | *Healthy Ageing* |
| Sarcopenic obesity | Sarcopenia together with obesity | *Undernutrition & Malnutrition* |
| Satiation | The fullness that builds during a meal and ends it; it sets meal size | *Appetite & Weight Regulation* |
| Satiety | The fullness after a meal that delays the next one; it sets how long until hunger returns | *Appetite & Weight Regulation* |
| Satiety cascade | The sequence in which fullness signals act over a meal: sensory, cognitive, gut and absorbed-nutrient signals | *Appetite & Weight Regulation* |
| Satiety peptides | Hormones released as food arrives, roughly in proportion to the calories eaten, that signal fullness: CCK, GLP-1, PYY and amylin | *Appetite & Weight Regulation* |
| Saturated fatty acid | A fatty acid with no double bonds: a straight chain that packs tightly, so the fat stays solid | *Macronutrients* |
| Scaling question | A question asking the patient to rate their confidence in a change from 0 to 10, and what makes it that number and not lower | *Behaviour-Change Counselling* |
| SCOFF | A five-question screen for eating disorders (vomiting, loss of control, recent weight loss, feeling fat, food dominating life); a screen, not a diagnosis | *Assessing Diet & Talking to Patients* |
| Scope of practice | The care a clinician's role allows them to deliver and be accountable for; knowing the science does not extend it | *Interprofessional Practice & Referral* |
| Scurvy | Vitamin C deficiency: bleeding, spongy gums, easy bruising, poor wound healing and corkscrew hairs, because collagen is not built | *Micronutrients, Hydration & Electrolytes* |
| Sebum | The oily secretion of the skin's sebaceous glands | *Evidence vs Hype* |
| Secondary active transport | Transport that spends a gradient built by a pump, as SGLT1 spends the sodium gradient to carry glucose into the enterocyte | *Digestion & Absorption* |
| Secondary structure | Local folding patterns in a protein chain: the α-helix and the β-sheet | *Macronutrients* |
| Secretin | A duodenal hormone, released when acid arrives, that increases pancreatic bicarbonate and reduces stomach acid | *Digestion & Absorption* |
| Secretory IgA | An antibody in breast milk that coats the infant's gut and blocks pathogens while the infant's own immunity matures | *Infancy & Early Childhood* |
| Segmentation | Back-and-forth squeezing that mixes the gut contents with digestive juices, mainly in the small intestine | *Digestion & Absorption* |
| Sensitisation | Priming of the immune system to react to a food | *Infancy & Early Childhood* |
| Sensitivity | The proportion of people with a condition whom a screening test correctly flags | *Assessing Diet & Talking to Patients* |
| Sensory-specific satiety | The fall in the pleasantness of a food as it is eaten, while a different food stays appealing | *Appetite & Weight Regulation* |
| SGLT1 (sodium–glucose cotransporter 1) | The transporter on the enterocyte that carries glucose into the cell alongside sodium | *Digestion & Absorption* |
| Short-chain fatty acids (SCFAs) | Acetate, propionate and butyrate: the main products of colonic fermentation, which fuel the colonic epithelium and act as signals elsewhere in the body | *Gut Microbiome* |
| Simulated patient | Someone (in this book, an AI model) who plays the patient in a practice consultation; not a real patient, and not a source of medical advice | *Everyday & Preventive Counselling* |
| Single-nutrient reductionism | The search for one villain nutrient or one "superfood", in place of attention to the whole diet | *Why Nutrition Matters* |
| Six pillars of health | The evidence-based behaviours, used alongside drugs and surgery, that prevent, treat and sometimes reverse chronic disease: nutrition, physical activity, restorative sleep, stress management, positive social connection and avoidance of risky substances | *Why Nutrition Matters* |
| SMART goal | A goal that is specific, measurable, achievable, relevant and time-bound | *Behaviour-Change Counselling* |
| Social isolation | The objective lack of contact with other people | *Healthy Ageing* |
| Social prescription | A family doctor's referral of a patient to a community programme, such as Health Promotion Board activities, Active Ageing Centres or SportSG | *Interprofessional Practice & Referral* |
| Sodium J-curve | The suggestion that very low salt intake is harmful; largely a measurement artefact | *Cardiovascular Disease & Hypertension* |
| Soluble fibre | Viscous fibre, as in oats, legumes and some fruit, that slows digestion and the glucose rise | *Macronutrients* |
| Specificity | The proportion of people without a condition whom a screening test correctly clears | *Assessing Diet & Talking to Patients* |
| Sphincter | A muscular one-way gate in the gut (lower oesophageal, pyloric, ileocaecal, anal) that stops contents moving backwards | *Digestion & Absorption* |
| Stages of change | A heuristic model that names a patient's points of readiness to change (including pre-contemplation, contemplation and preparation), used to tailor how the clinician talks; it does not predict success | *Behaviour-Change Counselling* |
| Standard drink | A reference serving containing about 10 g of alcohol, used in drinking guidance | *Adulthood & Working Life* |
| Starch | The main polysaccharide of rice, bread and potato: a mix of amylose and amylopectin | *Macronutrients* |
| Starvation-related malnutrition | Malnutrition from a pure intake deficit, without inflammation | *Undernutrition & Malnutrition* |
| Statin | A cholesterol-lowering drug | *Cardiovascular Disease & Hypertension* |
| Surrogate endpoint | A measured marker, such as blood pressure or a blood test, that stands in for a hard endpoint | *Evidence vs Hype* |
| Synbiotic | A combination of a probiotic and a prebiotic | *Gut Microbiome* |
| T-score | Bone density on a DXA scan, expressed in standard deviations from the young-adult peak; −2.5 or below defines osteoporosis | *Bone & Joint Health* |
| Tamoxifen | An anti-oestrogen drug used to treat oestrogen-receptor-positive breast cancer | *Menopause & Midlife Health* |
| Tau | A protein that accumulates in tangles inside neurons in neurodegeneration | *Brain Health & Dementia* |
| TCA cycle | The mitochondrial cycle (also called the citric acid or Krebs cycle) that fully oxidises acetyl-CoA from all three fuels to CO₂, capturing the energy on electron carriers | *Integrative Metabolism* |
| Teratogenic | Able to cause birth defects | *Micronutrients, Hydration & Electrolytes* |
| Terminal ileum | The last stretch of the small intestine, where bile salts are reclaimed and vitamin B12 is absorbed | *Digestion & Absorption* |
| Tertiary structure | The overall 3D fold of a protein chain | *Macronutrients* |
| Texture-modified food | Food whose texture is altered (for example minced or puréed) to make swallowing safer | *Healthy Ageing* |
| Thermic effect of food (TEF) | The energy cost of digesting, absorbing and processing a meal, about 10% of total energy expenditure; highest for protein | *Energy Balance* |
| Tiered dietitian pathway | The Healthier SG arrangement in which clinicians give first-line dietary advice and escalate complex cases to a registered dietitian | *Interprofessional Practice & Referral* |
| Time-restricted eating | Limiting eating to a daily window, as in "16:8"; it produces weight loss mainly by reducing energy intake | *Integrative Metabolism* |
| Tolerance | Acceptance of a food by the immune system, so that eating it causes no reaction | *Infancy & Early Childhood* |
| Tongue-thrust reflex | An infant reflex that pushes food out of the mouth; its loss is one sign of readiness for solids | *Infancy & Early Childhood* |
| Total diet replacement | A supervised low-calorie formula phase followed by structured food reintroduction, used in remission programmes, with medication adjusted by the programme's clinical team on day one | *Type 2 Diabetes* |
| Total energy expenditure (TEE) | The energy the body spends: basal metabolic rate plus the thermic effect of food plus physical activity | *Energy Balance* |
| Triglyceride | Three fatty acids esterified onto a glycerol backbone; the main form of dietary and stored fat | *Macronutrients* |
| Twin-cycle model | The model in which excess fat in the liver raises fasting glucose and fat in the pancreas impairs β-cell function, each cycle feeding the other | *Type 2 Diabetes* |
| Ultra-processed foods | Industrial formulations made largely from refined ingredients and additives, with little intact whole food | *Appetite & Weight Regulation* |
| Under-reporting | The systematic omission or shrinking of less-flattering foods and portions in self-reported intake, greater at higher body weight | *Assessing Diet & Talking to Patients* |
| Undernutrition | The deficit tail of malnutrition; what clinical screening and diagnosis mean by malnutrition | *Undernutrition & Malnutrition* |
| Universal advice | General nutrition guidance that is safe for almost anyone and that every clinician should give, such as My Healthy Plate | *Interprofessional Practice & Referral* |
| Universal screening | Testing every pregnancy instead of only women with risk factors; Singapore's approach to gestational diabetes | *Pregnancy & Lactation* |
| Unsaturated fatty acid | A fatty acid with one (monounsaturated) or more (polyunsaturated) double bonds | *Macronutrients* |
| Uraemia | The build-up in the blood of the wastes the kidney normally clears, such as urea; it blunts appetite | *Chronic Kidney Disease* |
| Urate | Uric acid; its crystals inflame the joint in gout | *Bone & Joint Health* |
| Vascular tone | How constricted the blood vessels are; higher tone raises blood pressure | *Cardiovascular Disease & Hypertension* |
| Villi | Finger-like projections of the small-intestinal lining that enlarge its absorptive surface | *Digestion & Absorption* |
| Vitamin K deficiency bleeding | Bleeding in newborns and young infants caused by too little vitamin K, prevented by a single vitamin K injection at birth | *Infancy & Early Childhood* |
| Waist circumference | A measure of central (visceral) fat that adds the metabolic risk information BMI misses | *Energy Balance* |
| Wanting | The motivational pull toward a food, driven by dopamine | *Appetite & Weight Regulation* |
| War on Diabetes | Singapore's national programme, launched in 2016, that treats diabetes as a population-scale problem | *Why Nutrition Matters* |
| Water-soluble vitamins | The B-complex vitamins and vitamin C: largely not stored (except B12), so they need regular intake | *Micronutrients, Hydration & Electrolytes* |
| Weight creep | The slow adult weight gain, of roughly 0.5–1 kg a year, that comes from a small, chronic energy surplus | *Adulthood & Working Life* |
| Weight cycling | Repeated weight loss and regain | *Adulthood & Working Life* |
| Weight-inclusive (care) | Care that anchors counselling on health behaviours and metabolic markers instead of on the scale alone | *Obesity & Metabolic Syndrome* |
| Weight-neutral language | Counselling language that centres on sustainable eating patterns and how the patient feels more than on body weight | *Behaviour-Change Counselling* |
| Weight stigma | Negative attitudes towards, and treatment of, people because of their weight, such as blame, shaming or disrespect | *Obesity & Metabolic Syndrome* |
| Wernicke's encephalopathy | A thiamine-deficiency emergency, classically in heavy drinkers, with confusion, unsteadiness and eye-movement problems; thiamine is given first | *Micronutrients, Hydration & Electrolytes* |
| Wholegrain | A grain that keeps its bran and germ, as brown rice does | *Macronutrients* |
| Xerophthalmia | Dryness of the eyes from vitamin A deficiency, between night blindness and corneal damage | *Micronutrients, Hydration & Electrolytes* |
